ICE: /api/_webrtc/ice returns TURN credentials only to signed-in callers, minted per app and user; anonymous callers get the STUN-only list unless features.ws_anonymous is true, and then share one credential per client address (an IPv6 client per /64).

Publishers: must be authed. /api/_broadcast/publish returns 401 `{error:'must be signed in to publish'}` to anonymous clients (a POST with neither a Bearer token nor a CSRF token gets 403 `{error:'invalid csrf'}` first).
Room rules: a slug matching a declared `ws_rooms:` pattern is a membership room - only members may publish or subscribe (admins bypass; anonymous viewers are refused there even with ws_anonymous).

Slug ownership: a live slug belongs to its publisher. The same user can re-publish it (reload, reconnect); another user gets 409 until the publisher has sent no heartbeat for three minutes (subscribes do not count as activity). Hand-rolled publishers must POST /api/_broadcast/heartbeat at least every minute.
Subscribers: respect features.ws_anonymous (same flag as /ws and /sse/events). Set features.ws_anonymous: true to let anon viewers subscribe; otherwise auth is required.

Stats: /api/_broadcast/stats/{slug} answers the same audience as subscribe (signed in unless features.ws_anonymous, a member of a ws_rooms slug, the publisher's tenant). Anyone else gets { live: false, viewers: 0 }, the answer for a slug that is not live, so a signed-out page of an app without ws_anonymous cannot show a stream as live.

Tenants: in an app with `groups:` (and features.ws_anonymous off) a slug's viewers must share the publisher's effective tenant, as bm.room rooms do; another tenant's user gets the same 404 as for a slug that isn't live (admins bypass). Each tenant has its own slug namespace: two tenants can both be live on `standup`, one tenant's publisher never gets 409 for another tenant's slug, and each tenant's viewers, stats and stop resolve their own. An admin outside the tenants reaches the most recently active stream with that slug. Apps without groups:, or with features.ws_anonymous, keep one app-wide namespace.

Streams marked `access.read: anon` in app.yaml are anon-readable for the metadata row (so anon viewers can list + render stream titles); the broadcast subscribe path is governed by features.ws_anonymous.
